entry.title: Culture, 1 August
entry.content:
Culture

Ariana Grande ‘Petal’ Album Review: The Pitfalls of Fame

NYT > Arts > Music

Album review of Ariana Grande's new record, "Petal". A pop culture heavyweight's album criticised for staying vague about the exact source of her disillusionment with fame.

Boy George Departs Jesus Christ Superstar After AI-Generated Pro-Israel Song

Vulture

Boy George has withdrawn from a West End revival of Jesus Christ Superstar. The exit follows backlash over an AI-generated pro-Israel reggae song he posted just days earlier.

A Great New Samurai Mystery From Kiyoshi Kurosawa

Vulture

A review of Kiyoshi Kurosawa's new film The Samurai and the Prisoner. The prolific Japanese director's first venture into the jidaigeki period-drama genre, described as a genuine find.

In the Lovely Wild Inside, Flaco the Owl Gets His Documentary

Vulture

A review of the documentary Wild Inside, about Flaco the escaped Central Park Zoo owl. Director Penny Lane turns the story into a portrait of the city and community the bird drew together, not just the animal itself.

De beuk erin: waarom Belgische punk zichzelf meteen afschafte en voor Electronic Body Music ging

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

Een stuk over hoe de Belgische punkscene van de late jaren zeventig zichzelf razendsnel ombuigde naar EBM en cold wave. Een eigenzinnige wending in de muziekgeschiedenis: België sloeg punk algauw over voor industrial en Electronic Body Music.

Bewezen in Lokeren: Diana Ross is nog steeds Boss ★★★★☆

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

Een concertrecensie van Diana Ross op de Lokerse Feesten. Zestig jaar hits en nog steeds, aldus de recensie, een feilloos geoliede show met de nodige glitter.

entry.title: Culture, 31 July
entry.content:
Culture

Glen Hansard, Frontman of Irish Band the Frames, Dies at 56

NYT > Arts > Music

An obituary of Glen Hansard, frontman of the Irish band the Frames. He won an Oscar for "Falling Slowly" from the film Once, and died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin at 56.

Kavinsky (1975-2026), de muzikant die een universum vol elektro, film en auto’s creëerde

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

Een portret van de overleden Franse dj Kavinsky. Meer dan muzikant zag hij zichzelf als schepper van een heel universum van elektro, film en auto's.

Jennifer Finch, Scalding Bassist for Alt-Rock Band L7, Dies at 59

NYT > Arts > Music

An obituary of Jennifer Finch, bassist for the alt-rock band L7. Often performing barefoot, she powered the feminist grunge band's breakout hit "Pretend We're Dead."

Ma Rainey, Mother of More Than Just Blues, Comes Alive on New Release

NYT > Arts > Music

A look at a new archival release of Ma Rainey recordings. Restored from private collections, it reveals a musical reach far wider than the blues label she's known for.

Domi and JD Beck Return With ‘Who Asked?’

NYT > Pop Culture

A review of Domi and JD Beck's second album, "Who Asked?" The virtuoso jazz-and-beyond duo returns with songs more intricate than before.

More Typos, Fewer Em Dashes: Writers Are Creating an Anti-AI ‘Literary Counterculture’

Culture Latest

A report on a new anti-AI style spreading among writers. Novelists, journalists and LinkedIn posters are deliberately keeping typos and dropping em dashes so as not to be mistaken for chatbots.

entry.title: Culture, 29 July
entry.content:
Culture

Christopher Nolan’s ‘Odyssey’ Has a Circe Problem

NYT > Movies

Essay on Christopher Nolan's new adaptation of the Odyssey. A major director's blockbuster take on Circe draws serious literary criticism.

The Odyssey’s Circe Is the Best Female Character Nolan Has Ever Written

Vulture

Counter-essay arguing Nolan actually nailed Circe. A direct rebuttal to the prevailing complaint about Nolan's Odyssey, making the case she is his best-written woman.

Eindelijk: Steven Soderbergh gunt Ian McKellen (87) nog eens een glorieuze hoofdrol ★★★★☆

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

Review of Steven Soderbergh's new film The Christophers. Ian McKellen and Michaela Coel face off as artist and forger in a dark comic character study from a major director.

Julian Casablancas Picked the Wrong Fights

Vulture

Critical take on the Strokes' new album Reality Awaits. A close reading of Julian Casablancas's diss track and the record surrounding it, timed to the band's 25th anniversary.

Linda Perhacs, Experimental Folk Singer, Is Reported Missing

NYT > Arts > Music

News report on folk singer Linda Perhacs. Friends say the influential psychedelic folk songwriter has been unreachable since leaving a care facility eight months ago.

Carly Simon Reveals She Has Parkinson’s Disease

NYT > Arts > Music

Carly Simon discloses a Parkinson's diagnosis. The songwriter also reveals skin cancer surgery and explains her recent withdrawal from public life.

entry.title: Culture, 27 July
entry.content:
Culture

‘Dread Beat an Blood’ Set Black Londoners’ Struggle to a Groove

NYT > Arts > Music

A restored 1979 documentary revisits Linton Kwesi Johnson's dub poetry. It traces how his verse set the struggles of Black Caribbean Londoners to a groove, turning protest into rhythm.

The Haunting Music in the ‘Odyssey’ Siren Scene Has Ancient Roots

NYT > Arts > Music

A look at the score behind the siren scene in Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey.' Ludwig Göransson dug up an ancient Greek instrument, the aulos, to make the sirens' pull sound genuinely tormenting.

The Strokes zijn ook op ‘Reality awaits’ te koppig om een memorabele rockplaat te maken ★★☆☆☆

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

Een recensie van het nieuwe album van The Strokes, 'Reality awaits'. De band bestookt haar eigen mythe met kille sciencefiction, maar vergeet ondertussen memorabele songs te schrijven.

“Ik druk gewoon op play en het publiek gaat uit zijn dak”: de topplaat van King Earthquake

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

Een gesprek met Erol Arrawak, alias King Earthquake, over zijn onvermijdelijke topnummer. Hij zou 'Horns man' zelf liever laten rusten, maar het publiek gaat elke keer uit zijn dak zodra het klinkt.

Jacques Tati zag een halve eeuw geleden al hoe komisch en absurd het moderne leven kan zijn

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

De films van Jacques Tati keren terug in de bioscoop. Met 'Mon oncle' en 'Playtime' zag Tati een halve eeuw geleden al hoe absurd het moderne leven kon worden, en dat blijkt nog steeds actueel.

Charli XCX Gave Us a Little More Music (and Fashion, and Film)

Vulture

Een stuk over Charli XCX's laatste uitloper van haar 'Music, Fashion, Film'-periode. Het is de post-credits scene van een cultureel moment dat al leek afgesloten, met nog meer muziek, mode en film erbovenop.

entry.title: Culture, 25 July
entry.content:
Culture

Charli XCX’s A.G. Cook Tribute Song Is Great

Vulture

A closer look at the Charli XCX song on her new album devoted entirely to her longtime producer A.G. Cook.

Within a spare 11-track record, a two-and-a-half-minute tribute to a key collaborator stands out as its emotional core.

Charli XCX Successfully Delivers the Anti-Brat

Vulture

A review of Charli XCX's new album Music, Fashion, Film.

The claim on the table is that this record is the deliberate opposite of the brat persona that made her a cultural juggernaut.

One of the Greatest of Films, Visconti’s White Nights, Is Back in Theaters

Vulture

Luchino Visconti's 1957 film White Nights returns to theatres.

A critic makes the case for a film Visconti made while caught between being neorealism's founder and its supposed betrayer.

Voor de punk was er punk: “Er zaten al barsten in het optimisme van de sixties”

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

A history of what came before punk, tracing the cracks already in sixties optimism.

Nugget collector and Patti Smith Group guitarist Lenny Kaye argues punk bands were less an invention than a clean sweep of what already existed.

Overlooked No More: Barbara Rubin, Teenage Filmmaker at the Heart of New York’s Underground

NYT > Arts > Music

A profile of Barbara Rubin, teenage filmmaker of the New York underground.

She made the landmark film Christmas on Earth and brought together Warhol, Ginsberg and Dylan, yet has gone largely unrecognised until now.

Freddy Cannon, Rocker Who Sang ‘Palisades Park,’ Dies at 89

NYT > Arts > Music

An obituary for Freddy Cannon, the rock and roller behind Palisades Park.

Known as Boom Boom, he turned his mother's poem into the hit Tallahassee Lassie and helped define early rock and roll's teenage sound.

entry.title: Culture, 24 July
entry.content:
Culture

How Conor Oberst Survived Teenage Rock Stardom

NYT > Arts > Music

A long profile of Conor Oberst on three decades as a cult singer-songwriter, his personal struggles and writing political songs under Trump.

A substantial piece on a songwriter whose confessional, piano-adjacent tradition sits close to his taste.

Bonnie Tyler, zangeres van ‘Total Eclipse of the Heart’ op 75-jarige leeftijd overleden

Muziek - KnackFocus

Bonnie Tyler, singer of 'Total Eclipse of the Heart', has died at 75.

An obituary of a musician he would know from the pop canon.

Van Baby Rose tot Joey Alexander: de pop- en jazzalbums van de week

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

De Standaard's weekly pick of the best pop and jazz albums, including Baby Rose and pianist Joey Alexander.

A quick weekly scan for new jazz and piano releases in his wheelhouse.

Een mix van piano en Perzische percussie, en een van de beste Franse pianisten: de beste klassieke albums van het moment

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

De Standaard's roundup of the best current classical albums, featuring a piano-and-Persian-percussion project and a leading French pianist.

Piano-centred classical picks that fit his listening habits.

De film ‘Los Domingos’ getuigt van zeldzame intellectuele nieuwsgierigheid

Film - KnackFocus

A review of the Spanish film Los domingos, about a teenage girl choosing a religious life against her family's wishes.

An arthouse title praised for real intellectual curiosity, worth reading before deciding to see it.

‘The Odyssey’ is een zeldzaam beest van een blockbuster

Film - KnackFocus

A Dutch-language review of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, weighing its scale against its shortcomings.

A critical assessment of a major director's new blockbuster, for someone who follows serious cinema writing.
